title: GTK2 observer and worker isolation validated on a private session bus

method.display: Fresh xvfb-run X11 server; no desktop or user X session used.
method.session_bus: Private dbus-daemon socket under the fixture directory; no SESSION_MANAGER or WAYLAND_DISPLAY inherited.
method.observer: Production theme_companion_bridge.watch() and its QProcess worker; the production GTK2 palette runtime and _GTK_READ_RCFILES sender ran unchanged.
method.gtkconfig: Private test service implementing the GTKConfig theme-name methods and exporting synthetic palette files only under the fixture profile. The observer received a private org.kde.kconfig.notify.ConfigChanged signal.
method.isolation_checks: Parent process asserted HOME, all XDG paths, private bus and X11 display. Each worker repeated these assertions before importing/calling the production bridge.

failed_fixture_attempts: R121 first run remained under private HOME/XDG/D-Bus, but its fake GTKConfig service lacked selected-theme.txt, so gtkTheme() returned FileNotFoundError and no palette update occurred. A diagnostic confirmed the missing fixture file. The root cause was fixed by creating selected-theme.txt before starting the service; the successful retry is in the evidence directory.
limits: KConfig notification was emitted by the fixture, and GTKConfig export was a private service implementation; this does not prove the installed kded6/KConfigWatcher/GTKConfig module chain itself.
GTK4 was exercised only because the production bridge synchronizes it alongside GTK2; no GTK4 fidelity claim is made.

The process printed a non-fatal GLib main-context teardown critical after the verified result; observer, worker, service, D-Bus and Xvfb exited. This is recorded as test-harness cleanup noise and is not hidden.
next: Consider a fully private kded6 + installed GTKConfig module fixture, after verifying it cannot join the user session bus or write outside ~/tempia; then audit the remaining GTK2 end-to-end gaps. Do not treat this as human fidelity approval or permission to modify the user profile.
